name: Zeruiah
description: Woman living at the time of United Monarchy

points: David asked Ahimelech the Hittite and Abishai the son of Zeruiah, the brother of Joab, Who will go down with me to Saul to the camp? and Abishai said, I will go down with thee; and they came to the people by night, and all lay sleeping.

note.label: 1 Samuel 26: David Spares Saul a Second Time

points: Asahel, one of the three sons of Zeruiah, was as light of foot as a wild roe, meaning he was fast, and he pursued Abner and would not turn aside. Abner warned him again and again to turn off and take another man's armor, not wanting to have to kill him and face Joab his brother.

note.label: 2 Samuel 2: David Anointed King Over Judah

points: David said he was weak that day though anointed king, and that the sons of Zeruiah were too hard for him, ruthless men he could not bring under; but the Lord would reward the doer of evil according to his wickedness. That payback came later through Solomon concerning Joab.

note.label: 2 Samuel 3: The House of David Waxes Stronger

points: Then said Abishai the son of Zeruiah unto the king, Why should this dead dog curse my lord the king? let me go over, I pray thee, and take off his head.

Abishai the son of Zeruiah asked why this dead dog should curse the king, and offered to go take off his head. But the king said, What have I to do with you, ye sons of Zeruiah? Let him curse, because the Most High hath said unto him, Curse David; who shall then say, Wherefore hast thou done so?

note.label: 2 Samuel 16: Ziba, Shimei's Cursing, and Absalom Defiles the Concubines

points: And the king said, What have I to do with you, ye sons of Zeruiah? so let him curse, because the Lord hath said unto him, Curse David. Who shall then say, Wherefore hast thou done so? So King David said, you know what, let this man curse me out. Now David is a king. His mighty men are ready to put this dude to death. But he says, let him be. He said it had to be the Lord that spoke unto him and told him to come and curse me.

Abishai and the sons of Zeruiah said Shimei should be put to death for cursing the Lord's anointed, but David rebuked them as adversaries, asking whether any man should be put to death that day in Israel when he knew he was king. He swore Shimei would not die. David understood grace long before the New Testament, for grace has always been around.

note.label: 2 Samuel 19: The King Returns to His House

points: The Philistines had war again with Israel, and David went down and waxed faint. Ishbi-benob, of the sons of the giant, thought to slay him, but Abishai the son of Zeruiah succoured him and killed the Philistine. Then the men of David swore that he should go no more out with them to battle, that he quench not the light of Israel; he was getting up in age and it was time to sit on the throne.

note.label: 2 Samuel 21: The Famine, the Gibeonites, and the Sons of the Giant

points: Jesse's sons are set down in order, with David named the seventh, and his sisters Zeruiah and Abigail.
The sons of Zeruiah, Abishai, Joab, and Asahel, are named, and Amasa the son of Abigail, whose father was Jether the Ishmaelite.

note.label: 1 Chronicles 2: The Sons of Israel and the Line of Judah

points: David said whoever smote the Jebusites first would be chief and captain. Joab the son of Zeruiah went up first and became chief.
